prose.summary: XR prototypers build quick virtual, augmented or mixed-reality experiences to test interaction and technical feasibility. They combine real-time engines, three-dimensional content and experimental design. The repository currently has no live jobs or detail file for this title.
prose.day_to_day: The work can include assembling scenes, scripting interactions, testing devices and changing prototypes after observation. Route evidence points to Unity, Unreal, C++, rendering and creative coding through adjacent roles. Without live openings, current employer workflows and device expectations are not measured.
prose.work_environment: XR prototyping is computer and device based, with testing tied to headsets or tracked spaces. Some work can be remote, but the empty live sample does not support a current location claim. Shared hardware and user testing may require lab or studio access.
prose.getting_in: Build a small prototype around one interaction question rather than a broad virtual world. Use Unity or Unreal, test on the target device and record comfort, performance and usability failures. Game development, technical art and three-dimensional work provide the closest adjacent evidence.
prose.ladder: Early prototypers build contained interactions and technical demonstrations. Responsibility can grow toward prototype strategy, engine systems, user testing and handoff into production. The path may branch into game development, technical art, interaction design or immersive product work.
prose.suits: This work fits people who enjoy fast experiments and can discard impressive work when it fails on a device or with users. It requires comfort across code, visuals and physical interaction. It is a poor fit if every prototype must become a polished product.
prose.misconceptions: XR prototyping is not mainly creating a beautiful virtual scene. The useful work tests interaction, comfort, performance and whether the concept deserves production investment.
prose.who_qualifies: Game developers, technical artists, game designers and three-dimensional modelers bring the closest route evidence. They need to show device-based interaction and prototype judgment. The absent live sample limits stronger qualification claims.
prose.what_the_numbers_miss: The missing live jobs and detail files leave current demand, tools and employer settings unmeasured. Device access and testing quality would remain important even in a larger sample.

steps.how: Test a specific interaction, spatial behavior or technical risk instead of building a vague immersive demo.
Use Unity or Unreal and keep the prototype small enough to change after each test.
Observe comfort, tracking, input and performance rather than judging only from a desktop preview.
Explain what the prototype proved, what failed and whether production work is justified.

faq.q: how do you become an XR prototyper?
faq.a: Build a small Unity or Unreal prototype around one spatial interaction question and test it on the target device. Show the decision produced by the experiment.

faq.q: do XR prototypers need to code?
faq.a: Usually. The adjacent evidence includes C++ and real-time engines, while scripting is needed to test interaction rather than display a static scene.

faq.q: what is the difference between XR prototyping and game development?
faq.a: XR prototyping tests immersive interaction and feasibility quickly, while game development carries systems and content toward a supported product. The tools overlap, but the delivery goals differ.
